issues.title: C86-19 — High: the implementation worker cannot implement or fence files inside submodules
issues.cause: The rewritten prompt emitter still permits only root-worktree Git commands and finishes with a root git add and commit. The workflow's implement-finalize role still snapshots, validates, and diffs only the root occurrence. For a task owning vendor/src/x.ts, root Git cannot stage the contents inside vendor; a submodule-only commit leaves root HEAD unchanged and is rejected; manually advancing the root gitlink makes the fence see only vendor, not vendor/src/x.ts. The apparent end-to-end test manually commits inside the submodule through a callback that the generated worker contract does not provide and declares ownership of vendor rather than the actual nested file.

locations.role: Worker instructions allow only root-worktree Git commands.
Implementation commit and fence validation inspect only the root occurrence.
The deterministic finalizer diffs only the root checkout.
Fixture manually performs the forbidden submodule commit and masks nested ownership behind the root gitlink.

issues.provingTest: Prepare a task whose only owned path is a real file below a submodule. Have the fake worker follow the literal generated instructions, edit that file, and attempt the prescribed commit; the current workflow cannot return done. As a fence negative control, manually commit an unowned file inside the submodule and its root gitlink; a correct implementation reports the normalized nested path, while the current code reports only the gitlink.
suggestedFixApproach: Build an occurrence-aware ownership map. Snapshot, stage, commit, and diff owned paths in each occurrence deepest-first, then commit changed gitlinks in their parents.

Normalize every occurrence-local changed path back to its root-relative task path before fence comparison. Generate explicit git -C <occurrence-checkout> instructions for the worker instead of forbidding them.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: The manifest already supplies occurrence IDs, checkout paths, depths, and parent relationships for occurrence-aware ownership.
Merge already walks occurrences deepest-first and commits changed gitlinks in parents.

acceptanceCriteria: The literal worker contract can stage and commit an owned file below a submodule.
Implementation snapshots and diffs cover every owned occurrence and normalize local paths to root-relative task paths.
An unowned nested edit is reported as the nested path, and focused nested-worktree tests pass.

remainingMinimalExample.code: test('implement commits and fences a file owned below a submodule', async () => { /* assert vendor/src/x.ts */ })

issues.title: C86-20 — High: a partial deepest-first merge is misclassified as a zero-progress lap
issues.cause: mergeTaskDeepestFirst may successfully move a source submodule and then fail its parent. The workflow returns the task as failed, recordStageOutcome increments mergedThisLap only for a completely merged task, and shouldEndQueue returns stuck when that count is zero. The spec intentionally keeps earlier source-layer merges, so the retry would not run against the same source state; stopping loses a potentially recoverable task.

locations.role: A child source layer can merge before a later parent layer fails.
A partially completed deepest-first walk is returned as a failed task.
The rewritten workflow forwards the failed merge result without recording source-layer progress.
Queue progress counts only fully merged tasks and declares the partial lap stuck.

issues.provingTest: Use a nested fixture in which the child source merge succeeds and the parent merge fails. Consume the real workflow envelope, prove the child source branch moved, and assert that the current queue has mergedThisLap equal to zero and reports stuck. The corrected queue must begin another lap, subject to the normal lap ceiling, because source progress occurred.
suggestedFixApproach: Track source-layer progress separately from fully merged task count, for example sourceProgressThisLap.
Set it when a failed merge result has a completed layer with status merged, reset it in beginNextLap, and apply the zero-progress exit only when neither a task nor any source layer moved.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: mergeTaskDeepestFirst already retains completedLayers when a later parent layer fails.
The queue already tracks per-lap full-task progress, carryover, and the lap ceiling.

acceptanceCriteria: A failed merge envelope records whether any source layer merged during the attempt.
The queue is stuck only when neither a task nor a source layer moved and failures remain.
beginNextLap resets source progress, and a child-merged/parent-failed regression begins another lap under the existing ceiling.

resolvedBoundaryExample.code:
return { stage: 'merge', status, completedLayers, parentResult }
// completedLayers retains child layers that moved before the parent failed.

issues.title: C86-21 — High: unexpected rebase/merge exceptions reject the workflow instead of entering the retry queue
issues.cause: The rewrite moved Git and filesystem operations into emitter roles but did not make their failure contract total. A failed merge emitter is retried and eventually becomes the generic merge-driver-no-result envelope, losing the concrete operational reason. A failed rebase-walk or parent-rebase emitter returns no agent result and the workflow explicitly throws, so that stage still rejects with no status/lastFailure envelope for consumeTaskWorkflowResult. The task can therefore remain unqueued and unreported, contrary to tasks 149 and 153.

locations.role: Missing emitter results throw from rebase or degrade to a generic merge failure.
Emitter roles execute throwing rebase, merge, close, ref, and cleanup operations.

issues.provingTest: Make the rebase-walk emitter exit nonzero after a deterministic Git or ref failure and have the workflow agent return no result, as it does when the command produces no valid result instructions. The current workflow retries and then throws instead of returning a blocked envelope. Separately create a leaf ref named refs/taskTools/merge-intents so merge persistence creation fails; the merge path returns only a generic driver-no-result reason. The fixed results must carry the concrete operational reason through queue carryover and reporting. A nested variant should merge the child first and trigger the failure only in the parent, retaining C86-20 progress data.
suggestedFixApproach: Make the rebase and merge primitives total and return typed failure reports, or wrap every stage-level primitive call in try/catch.

Normalize operational exceptions to a nonempty stage-specific lastFailure while preserving completedLayers, source-progress information, conflict paths, and merged-but-not-closed semantics once the root merge has landed.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: concreteMergeStageFailure already converts structured merge failures into nonempty actionable reasons.
Queue consumption already retains ordinary blocked and merged-but-not-closed failures.

acceptanceCriteria: Every rebase-walk, parent-rebase, and merge operational exception becomes a typed workflow result.
lastFailure keeps the concrete operational reason and preserves completed layers, conflicts, source progress, and merged-but-not-closed state.
Queue reporting accepts all normalized failure shapes, including child progress followed by parent failure.

remainingMinimalExample.code: if (!layerWalk) return { stage: 'rebase-test', task: N, status: 'blocked', lastFailure: 'rebase-walk driver returned no result' }

issues.title: C86-22 — High: missingFiles from the third/final plan review is ignored
issues.cause: runPlan performs the first verification, decrements reviewRounds, and handles rejected output only while reviewRounds is greater than zero. It makes three verifier calls but processes only the first two rejections. A third response containing missingFiles exits the loop and implementation begins with the old file fence and unrepaired plan. Task 136 requires widening and replanning whenever verification returns nonempty missingFiles and defines no final-round exception.

locations.role: The loop exits before processing the third verifier rejection.

issues.provingTest: Script verifier responses as rejected with ordinary fixes, rejected with ordinary fixes, then rejected with missingFiles containing b.ts. Assert that the authoritative task record, run-arguments snapshot, rewritten plan and brief, and implementer prompt all include b.ts. They currently do not.
suggestedFixApproach: Model each of the three rounds as verify followed by processing that result.

On a rejected third review, still widen and replan or apply feedback, but do not invoke a fourth verifier. Preserve the final verifier notes and verdict for the user gate so the unverified final repair remains visible.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: widenFilesAndReplan already persists missing files, refreshes the in-memory fence, and replans before another review.
The authoritative widening mutation is already locked and updates the run-arguments snapshot.

acceptanceCriteria: Each of the three review rounds is modeled as verify followed by processing that verifier result.
A final-round missingFiles rejection widens authoritative task state and repairs the plan without invoking a fourth verifier.
Final verifier notes and verdict remain visible to the approval gate when the repaired plan is not reviewed again.
The final implementer prompt, brief, plan, and ownership fence all include files introduced by the third review.

remainingMinimalExample.code: test('third rejected review still widens and repairs without a fourth verification', async () => { /* assert b.ts reaches task state, brief, plan, and worker */ })

issues.title: C86-23 — High: accepted proposed tasks bypass the task-state lock and can race with close
issues.cause: The gate can invoke create-task while tail workflows are concurrently merging and closing. The generated create-task brief directs its agent to append to tasks.json directly. closeTasks holds the shared lock and publishes a whole-file replacement, but an editor that ignores that lock can overwrite the close or be overwritten by it, resurrecting a closed task or losing the new task.

locations.role: Accepted proposals may invoke create-task while tail workflows are active.
The skill tells an agent to edit tasks.json directly without the task-state mutex.
Close uses a locked whole-file replacement that can race with the unlocked editor.

issues.provingTest: In two real processes, make the append process read tasks.json and pause. Let closeTasks acquire the lock, archive and remove task A, and publish. Resume the stale append of task B and prove A is resurrected. Add the reverse ordering and prove B can be lost under the current direct-editor protocol.
suggestedFixApproach: Add a programmatic task-append command that resolves the authoritative project root, acquires withTaskStateLock, rereads current state, allocates the number, appends, and atomically publishes.
Make the create-task skill gather fields but call that command; it must never write tasks.json directly. Test both orderings with real processes and an acknowledged inside-lock barrier.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: withTaskStateLock and writeJsonAtomically are the established transaction boundary for task-state writers.
Close already rereads and publishes task state while holding that mutex.

acceptanceCriteria: create-task calls one programmatic append operation and never directly edits tasks.json.
Append resolves authoritative state, locks, rereads, allocates, and atomically publishes inside one transaction.
Deterministic real-process tests cover append-first and close-first without resurrection or loss.

resolvedBoundaryExample.code:
const pair = resolveTaskFiles(projectRoot)
return withTaskStateLock(pair.tasksPath, () => closeTasksLocked(taskNumbers, closureNote, pair, commitHashes))

remainingMinimalExample.code: Send the task draft to appendTask on quoted-heredoc stdin; never edit tasks.json directly.

issues.title: C86-25 — High: deleting tracked implementation notes still satisfies the done guard
issues.cause: The unstaged attempt now blocks zero-commit, notes-only, and owned-change-without-notes done results, but it treats the expected notes pathname's presence in git diff --name-only base..HEAD as proof that the notes artifact was committed. A deletion also appears in that path list, so a worker starting from a checkout with tracked implementation notes can delete them, commit an owned-file change, report done, and pass with no required notes file in HEAD.

locations.role: Completion checks changedPaths membership but has no signal proving that the notes path exists as a tracked file in finalized HEAD.
The finalizer returns only headOid and name-only changes, which cannot distinguish a notes-file addition/modification from its deletion.
New coverage proves notes-only and never-created-notes rejection but does not exercise deletion of notes already tracked at the implementation-stage base.

issues.provingTest: Before launching a production-shaped implement stage, commit plans/task-N-implementation-notes.md into the prepared task worktree so it exists at the captured base. Have the worker delete that file, change and commit an owned source path, and return done. The current attempted guard returns done because changedPaths contains both paths; the corrected result is blocked with the missing-notes reason, and git cat-file -e HEAD:plans/task-N-implementation-notes.md fails as the negative control.
suggestedFixApproach: Extend implement-finalize to return a deterministic tracked-at-HEAD boolean for the exact expected notes path, using a Git tree query rather than worktree existence alone.

Require both changedPaths membership and tracked-at-HEAD presence before accepting done; retain the distinct notes-only, never-created-notes, zero-commit, and ownership-fence guards. Add the pre-existing-notes deletion regression.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: The unstaged attempt correctly snapshots HEAD and blocks zero-commit, notes-only, and never-created-notes done results; preserve those guards while adding artifact presence.
The worker contract names the exact notes path, and implement-finalize is the deterministic Git boundary that should verify it in HEAD.

acceptanceCriteria: Done requires the exact implementation-notes path to be changed in the commit range and present as a tracked file in finalized HEAD.
Deleting a notes file that existed at the implementation-stage base is blocked with the missing-notes reason even when an owned implementation path was committed.
The zero-commit, notes-only, never-created-notes, and ownership-fence behavior remains intact with deterministic workflow-level coverage.

issues.title: C86-26 — High: emitter roles reload stale ownership from the private worktree and undo widening
issues.cause: The emitter's loadPreparedTask resolves and reads tasks.json under WORKTREE. Widening correctly updates authoritative state under SOURCE_ROOT and briefly writes a widened worktree brief, but the next plan or verify role calls loadPreparedTask again, reloads the stale private task record, overwrites the widened brief, and emits the old ownership list. The workflow's in-memory preparedTask.files update is not passed to the emitter. A separately launched implement stage has the same stale-fence defect.

locations.role: Every role reloads and rewrites task context from the stale worktree task file.
The workflow updates ownership only in memory, while subsequent emitter calls reload their own stale copy.
Widening correctly updates authoritative source state rather than the private checkout.

issues.provingTest: Prepare a task owning a.ts. Drive a rejected verifier response with missingFiles containing b.ts. Assert that widen-files updates authoritative tasks.json, then capture the immediately following replanner and verifier prompts: both must include b.ts and the regenerated brief must retain it. The current plan role reloads the private a.ts-only record and overwrites the widened brief. Also launch a fresh implement stage and assert that its prompt and returned fence include b.ts; current behavior reloads only a.ts.
suggestedFixApproach: Load the current task record using resolveTaskFiles(SOURCE_ROOT), while continuing to place the task brief, plan, notes, Git operations, and edits under WORKTREE.
Represent authoritative task-state root and task checkout root as separate fields so later code cannot accidentally use one for the other.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: Widening already resolves task files from SOURCE_ROOT and atomically updates authoritative tasks.json plus the run snapshot.
Worktree-local brief, plan, notes, Git, and edit paths are already rooted under WORKTREE and should remain there.

acceptanceCriteria: Every emitter role reads the current task record from authoritative SOURCE_ROOT task state.
Brief, plan, notes, Git operations, and source edits remain rooted in the private WORKTREE.
A widen-files result survives the immediately following replan, verify, and separately launched implement roles.
Types distinguish taskStateRoot from checkoutRoot so the roots cannot be accidentally interchanged.

remainingMinimalExample.code: test('widened ownership survives replanning, verification, and a fresh implement stage', async () => { /* assert b.ts in every emitted prompt and fence */ })
